newsitem.title: UK: Bank of England to push for rate hike-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Bank of England to push for rate hike-newspaper.

text.p: The Bank of England is to press for an immediate rise in interest rates when its quarterly inflation report is released next week, The Guardian newspaper said on Saturday.

It said the bank would like to see a half-percentage point increase from the current six percent but accepts that the short-term inflation outlook means that finance minister Kenneth Clarke is unlikely to agree in the run-up to a general election that must be held by May 22 at the latest.

The paper said the bank has become so frustrated by the finance minister's refusal to raise rates that it is now looking sympathetically at proposals by the opposition Labour Party to shake up the mechanism for setting interest rates.

Senior bank officials were said to be warming to Labour finance spokesman Gordon Brown's plan to create a policy forum inside the bank which would dilute the power of the Chancellor of the Exchequer and the bank governor.
The paper said this monetary policy committee could include three powerful outsiders. One of these might be an overseas financial figure, possibly former Bundesbank president Karl Otto Pohl.
